title: Best Coffee Grinders UK
short: Six hand and electric coffee grinders compared on grind consistency, adjustability, ease of cleaning and value.
intro: Freshly ground beans beat pre-ground coffee, but grinders vary hugely in how finely, evenly and easily they grind. This guide is based on Expert Reviews' tested roundup, where each grinder was set up for a range of brewing methods (coarse for cafetieres, medium for filter, fine for espresso) using freshly roasted beans, with attention to grind consistency, ease of use and cleaning, hopper capacity and extras. The guide dates from 2024, so prices are as reviewed.

products.name: Skerton Pro Coffee Grinder
products.best_for: Anyone who wants a compact, affordable hand grinder and doesn't mind the effort
products.key_spec: Hand grinder, ceramic burrs, 60g hopper, adjustable grind, sealable glass container
products.summary: Expert Reviews rate it perhaps the best hand grinder around. Despite its compact size the hopper holds up to 60g of beans, and compared with the earlier Skerton Plus it has improved grind adjustment, a thicker handle and an anti-slip rubber grip. The obvious downside is that you grind by hand, which can be arduous or a wrist workout depending on your view.
pros: Improved grind adjustment and anti-slip grip over the Skerton Plus
Grind container can be sealed with the included lid
cons: You have to grind by hand

products.name: Coffee Grinder (manual)
products.best_for: Anyone who wants a slim hand grinder that switches grind size easily
products.key_spec: Hand grinder, six grind levels via a dial, about 18g hopper
products.summary: Expert Reviews found a neat, compact hand grinder with a simple dial for six preset grind levels, much easier than the Hario's screw adjustment, though the Hario allows finer tweaks. It holds only about 18g of beans and must be kept upright in the hands or beans can spill. At £59 it's not the cheapest manual grinder and the Hario beats it on capacity for less.
pros: Preset levels make it easy to judge coarseness
cons: Small hopper, only about 18g of beans
Must be kept upright or beans can spill

products.name: Expert GVX231 Burr Coffee Grinder
products.best_for: Espresso drinkers on a limited budget
products.key_spec: Electric burr grinder, 17 grind levels, 2 to 12 cup dial, 225g hopper with airtight lid
products.summary: Expert Reviews found about as affordable as a decent burr grinder gets: compact, quick and very easy to use, with a removable upper burr for easy cleaning. Unlike many budget grinders it delivers a fine espresso grind, but it struggles at the coarse end, with some users unable to get a coarse grind.
pros: Fine espresso grind, unusual at this price
Compact, quick and very easy to use
Removable upper burr for easy cleaning
cons: Struggles to deliver a coarse grind
products.search: Krups Expert GVX231 burr coffee grinder

products.name: Dose Control Pro
products.best_for: Anyone who wants control from coarse French press to ultra-fine espresso
products.key_spec: 60 grind settings, conical stainless steel burrs, 340g hopper, portafilter cradles
products.summary: Expert Reviews call it a versatile coffee-drinker's dream and the best bang-per-buck grinder they've used: 60 settings from coarse French press to ultra-fine espresso, easy to use and clean, with two portafilter cradle sizes. One downside they found is that with single cups it leaves some old grounds in the grind chamber.
pros: 60 grind settings from coarse to ultra-fine
Incredibly good value for what it does
cons: Leaves some old grounds in the grind chamber with single cups
products.search: Sage Dose Control Pro coffee grinder

products.name: Sette 270
products.best_for: Coffee connoisseurs who want uniform grounds and accurate dosing
products.key_spec: 30 macro plus 9 micro grind positions, LCD and timer, 275g hopper, doses to within 0.5g
products.summary: Expert Reviews found a sleek, fast, easy-to-use grinder that delivers nearly flawless, uniform grounds and always doses within 0.5g. It's a real coffee connoisseur's machine, but very noisy and fairly pricey, so not for everyone.

products.name: DBM8U Burr Mill
products.best_for: Cold brew, cafetière and percolator drinkers who want an even coarse grind
products.key_spec: 18 grind settings, 4 to 18 cup selector, auto shut-off, dishwasher-safe parts, 250g hopper, 5-year guarantee
products.summary: Expert Reviews found a workhorse that churns out a consistently even coarse grind, ideal for cold brew, percolator and French press, with all removable parts dishwasher-safe and a five-year guarantee. It does less well on finer espresso grounds, so espresso drinkers should look at a pricier machine.
cons: Less good at fine espresso grounds
products.search: Cuisinart DBM8U burr mill coffee grinder

guide.a: Expert Reviews recommends a burr grinder for consistency and quality, especially if you spend a lot on beans. Blade grinders are the budget option, but automatic burr grinders start at around £35, and all the electric models here use burrs.

guide.q: Which grinder is best for espresso?
guide.a: Espresso needs a fine, even grind and many budget burr grinders can't manage it. Of these, the Krups Expert delivers a fine espresso grind cheaply, the Sage Dose Control Pro covers ultra-fine with 60 settings, and the Baratza Sette 270 is the precision pick. The Cuisinart is weaker at fine grounds.

guide.q: Is a manual grinder worth it?
guide.a: Hand grinders like the Hario Skerton Pro are an affordable alternative to electric grinders and compact, but you have to grind by hand. The Lavazza is easier to adjust but holds only about 18g of beans, so both suit one or two cups at a time.

guide.q: What grind size for cold brew?
guide.a: Cold brew needs a coarse grind for easier filtration, sweetness and less bitterness, and fine grounds are best avoided. The Cuisinart DBM8U is Expert Reviews' pick for this and is also good for percolators, French presses and cafetières.
